A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAMoVAR work. All 16 pages of v1 and 20 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original synthetic VAR experiments and real-world forecasting results. The appendix includes component ablations, five-seed results and computational-cost measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains the original synthetic experiments, forecasting benchmarks, ablations, seed comparisons and computational-cost results.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same architecture, ARX tokenization, query/value construction, RMSNorm, shortcuts and structural projection. The new appendices analyze existing components rather than introduce a changed procedure.

E1.justification: The synthetic VAR task and reported Weather, Solar, ECL, ETT, Traffic and PEMS coverage are unchanged. The PEMS07 exclusion is also retained; no new evaluated domain or test scenario appears.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain LinTrans, FixedVAR, CATS, iTransformer, FITS, PatchTST, DLinear and Encformer, including the same computational-cost subset. Newly discussed related methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: New Appendix A.7.2 prints the width rule as floor(32*sqrt(C)), differing from the previous 32*floor(sqrt(C)). However, v2 retains the old rule elsewhere and the d=64 example for C=7. This is an inconsistent change in the reported setting, not evidence of rerun experiments; other protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The component, head-count and depth ablations in Tables 2 and 4–6 are unchanged, as are the synthetic interpretability case studies. Appendices A.8–A.9 add theoretical arguments, not new robustness experiments.

E5.justification: Table 7 retains the same five runs with seeds 2023–2027 and the same reporting practice. Neither version adds confidence intervals, significance tests or another empirical uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–8 match, and the empirical figures are retained. For example, Table 1 reports the same ETTh1 average MSE of 0.401 for SAMoVAR and 0.419 for LinTrans.

T1.justification: Beyond v1's VAR derivations and informal pruning rationale, v2 adds a computational-complexity proposition and proof in A.7.1, an RMSNorm path-bound argument in A.8, and a high-dimensional orthogonality probability argument in A.9. These substantially expand the formal analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same VAR interpretation, structural-alignment contribution, SAMoVAR proposal and accuracy, interpretability and efficiency claims. The added appendix arguments do not redefine the core contributions.

C2.justification: A.7.2 newly attributes part of the efficiency advantage to narrower hidden dimensions and explains why FixedVAR can have more parameters but fewer FLOPs. The limitations concerning foundation-model scale and applications beyond forecasting remain unchanged.

D1.justification: A.7.2 expands documentation of the existing Table 8 comparison, including typical baseline widths of 128/256 and their relationship to parameter counts. The original implementation details, hardware, training instructions and code-access link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.3 substantially expands the earlier introduction/background discussion into a dedicated survey of forecasting and linear attention. Added literature includes LSTM, DeepAR, Time-LLM, foundation forecasting, Crossformer and MEGA, broadening the research context without changing evaluated comparators.

P1.justification: The main argument remains largely verbatim. Local terminology clarifications, an Impact Statement, new appendix subsections, appendix renumbering and updated conference/correspondence information produce a limited structural and editorial revision.

P2.justification: The same 13 figures and eight tables retain their content and captions. Table 1 moves from page 7 to page 8, and appendix displays are regrouped and interleaved with the new complexity proof, changing placement and pagination.

improvement.justification: A.3 and A.7 add useful context and efficiency explanations, but the new formal support has material weaknesses. A.8 turns an approximate initialization argument into a unit path bound and training-stability guarantee without establishing the necessary constraints, while A.7.2 introduces an inconsistent width formula. With empirical evidence unchanged, the explanatory gains and new rigor and reproducibility problems leave the net quality direction uncertain.
